sections.what_happened: CEC official count has begun: Ynetnews reports the CEC announced official results are being released, with results from 15 polling stations received, representing 2,679 voters; Al Jazeera liveblog (Channel 12) reports 15 polling stations / 2,670 votes as of 12:18am Israel time (22:18 GMT Oct 27). Poliwave's tracker disagrees on the early partial (0.3% of polls, 14,386 valid votes, updated 1:04am GMT+2) -- early trackers conflict, and neither partial supports any seat projection. Exit-poll picture unchanged and now Reuters-confirmed: change bloc 52-53 vs Netanyahu bloc 50, Arab-led parties 17-18, Likud largest single party 24-25, neither bloc at 61. Reuters adds the stalemate may keep Netanyahu in caretaker office while coalition talks run, and Eisenkot has all but ruled out governing with the Arab parties. The Times: President Herzog must choose who to ask first -- Netanyahu as largest-party leader or Eisenkot as largest-bloc leader. Turnout 77.7% (5.69m of 7.33m eligible, CEC via Al Jazeera) stands.
sections.what_verified: Exit-poll bloc totals converge across Kan 11/Channel 12/Channel 13 as carried by Reuters, Ynetnews, Al Jazeera and Times of Israel; CEC count-begun confirmed by CEC statement via Ynetnews and Channel 12 via Al Jazeera liveblog. Korea Times/Rappler carry the same Reuters wire = 1 family, not 2.
sections.what_disputed: Channel 14 (pro-Netanyahu) outlier: Netanyahu bloc 60, change bloc 43. thepetek.com tracker claims 'All ballots counted. The Netanyahu bloc finishes with 75 seats' -- CONTRADICTED by the CEC/Ynetnews partial (15 stations only) and by thepetek's own timeline ('~08:00 about 90% counted', double-envelope Oct 29); treat as a premature/misleading tracker, NOT a result. Poliwave (14,386 valid votes) vs Ynet/CEC (2,679 voters) early-partial discrepancy shows trackers are not yet in sync; no seat inference may be drawn from partials. USA Today reports turnout 'at least 80%' vs CEC 77.7% -- CEC figure prevails.
sections.why_matters: The count has started -- and it changes nothing yet: 15 stations in, the deadlock stands, and the only question left is who Herzog calls first and whether Eisenkot breaks his own red line on the Arab parties.

totw_analysis: Our read: The count has started -- and it changes nothing yet: 15 stations in, the deadlock stands, and the only question left is who Herzog calls first and whether Eisenkot breaks his own red line on the Arab parties. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Minority government with Arab-party support vs Netanyahu caretaker vs new elections -- Eisenkot leads the bloc but has ruled out the Arab parties (17-18 seats) whose votes are the only arithmetic route to 61; social threads argue Eisenkot is 'no different' from Netanyahu, and whether a caretaker Netanyahu is the real winner of a deadlock.
